content:
I have two notations for dealing with semantics:

class Semantics α β where
  sem : α -> β


namespace Semantics

scoped notation:1000 "Sem""⟦ " x " ⟧" => Semantics.sem x
scoped notation:1000 "["B"]""Sem""⟦ " x " ⟧" => @Semantics.sem _ B _ x

end Semantics

They are essentially the same, but the second allows you to explicitly specify the semantic domain we are working in - useful when it's ambiguous. I'd like to keep both around, because often lean is able to infer the domain, but when printing it's preferable by far to use the second - otherwise you can end up with two terms of different types with very similar representations.

However, as far as I am able to find, there's no easy way to tell lean which notation to prefer in pretty printing. Does anyone have any tips?
Pretty-printing is customisable in Lean. You can write your own delaborator (search for Delab) that inspects the B argument and determines whether it should be printed explicitly or not.

Although this is theoretically possible, no one has written such a delaborator AFAIA, even though mathlib is in dire need of many such! Good luck distinguishing docs#measurable_id and docs#measurable_id'' without looking at the source code, for example.
If you do manage to write such a delaborator, please please please PR (the suitably modified version of) it to mathlib :-)
We have delaborators for Continuous and IsOpen and such! But I don't think they worked well on examples I encountered in the wild.
